overview: In 2009 Congress approved a water rights settlement with the Shoshone-Paiute Tribes of the Duck Valley Reservation, on the Idaho-Nevada border, which included a $9 million development fund for the tribes. This bill would make what it calls a technical correction by allowing additional payments into that fund from 2027 through 2033. The extra amount is capped at the interest, compounded daily at a short-term Treasury rate, that the fund's balance would have earned over a past period ending in January 2016 if it had been invested under federal Indian trust fund rules. Any such payments would require Congress to provide the money in spending bills, and would come out of funds the Interior Department already uses to carry out Indian water rights settlements. As of October 29, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say the tribes should receive the investment earnings their settlement money would have made, and that paying them makes good on a deal the federal government already agreed to.
against: Critics say the bill adds new spending to a settlement that was meant to be final, and that paying it from existing water settlement funds could leave less money for other tribes' settlements.
